articles.title: Wembanyama’s Warning: Spurs star guarantees MVP-caliber season
articles.standfirst: Wembanyama makes bold MVP claim while reflecting on Spurs' NBA Finals defeat
articles.summary: Wembanyama makes bold MVP claim while reflecting on Spurs' NBA Finals defeat
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama isn't hiding his ambitions heading into the 2026-27 NBA campaign. The San Antonio Spurs superstar believes he's ready to take another significant step forward and has made it clear that winning the league's Most Valuable Player award is firmly on his agenda.

During an upcoming interview with CBS' 60 Minutes, the French center delivers a confident prediction about his individual prospects.

When discussing last season's MVP race, Wembanyama offered a straightforward response: “I should win it this year though.”

The statement shows the enormous expectations surrounding the 23-year-old after an outstanding third season in the league. Wembanyama helped guide San Antonio to the 2026 NBA Finals, although the Spurs ultimately lost 4-1 to the New York Knicks.

He also finished second in MVP voting behind Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander .

Despite missing out on the league's biggest individual honor, Wembanyama collected his first Defensive Player of the Year award and earned All-NBA recognition.

His remarkable combination of size, athleticism, defensive instincts and offensive versatility has established him as one of basketball's most exciting young talents.

The Spurs are also entering the new campaign with championship expectations, having emerged as favorites in early projections for the 2027 NBA Finals. Wembanyama's individual ambitions are therefore closely connected to the franchise's hopes of building on last season's playoff success.

Having already demonstrated his ability to influence games at both ends of the court, the Frenchman will be looking to deliver greater consistency and help San Antonio compete for another championship.

Winning MVP would further strengthen his position among the NBA's elite players.

Wembanyama reflects on his villain reputation after NBA Finals

The upcoming 60 Minutes interview, conducted by Jon Wertheim , also explores how Wembanyama handled the changing perception of his personality during the postseason.

For much of his NBA career, the Frenchman was celebrated for his extraordinary performances and spectacular highlights. However, several physical incidents during the playoffs brought criticism from opposing players and supporters.

An elbow involving Minnesota Timberwolves center Naz Reid and a confrontation with Knicks guard Jalen Brunson contributed to Wembanyama receiving a villain label, particularly among New York fans.

Asked whether that portrayal bothered him, Wembanyama explained that he wasn't paying attention to outside criticism while competing in the Finals.

“No, it didn't because I'm not paying attention to this-- during the Finals. I don't think any player on either team really is,” said Wembanyama .

He also acknowledged that the postseason exposed some of his competitive limits.

“It showed my limits more than anything else. Going out there, you need to play basketball. You don't need to beat the s*** out of people. [laughs] If you wanna win, at least,” he added.

That recognition could prove important as he continues developing into a leader for San Antonio. His talent has already placed him among the league's biggest stars, but managing emotions during high-pressure contests remains another challenge.

With the 2026-27 season underway, Wembanyama has made his objective unmistakable as he's determined to turn his confident prediction into reality while helping the Spurs pursue another championship.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama dresses up as iconic video game character for Halloween stadium entrance
articles.standfirst: Wemby is no longer Slender Man or No-Face, and is now a legendary monster hunter.
articles.summary: Wemby is no longer Slender Man or No-Face, and is now a legendary monster hunter.
articles.body:
Halloween is the perfect time for professional athletes to show a different side of themselves. Fans always see the hard-noses, sports-focused version of athletes, but many of them are just regular people with the same type of hobbies and interests as the masses.

Victor Wembanyama would certainly say that defines him as well. As fans have seen from some of his Halloween costumes, Wemby is a man of culture. He acknowledged the memes made about him for his first epic costume, that of Slender Man in 2023. He followed that up with No-Face (Kaonashi) in 2024.

Victor Wembanyama dresses up as Geralt of Rivia from The Witcher for Halloween

This year, Wembanyama went in a much different direction, but it was still as epic as the other two. For 2026, Wemby showed up to the stadium on Halloween night decked out as Geralt of Rivia , from the legendary The Witcher fantasy series.

Geralt became famous worldwide following the incredible success and critical acclaim of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , a game published by Polish video game developer CD Projekt Red . Andrzej Sapkowski created Geralt for his The Witcher fantasy novel series, which follows his experiences as a monster-hunting witcher .

Netflix later adapted some of Sapkowski’s books for a TV show, which starred Henry Cavill as Geralt of Rivia. Wemby would simply be too tall to be a real witcher, but he certainly crushed his costume design.

articles.body:
LeBron James needed every last second to beat Jimmy Donaldson , better known as MrBeast , in a charity three-point contest that came down to one basket as the veteran Philadelphia 76ers player won 6-5, earning a $100,000 donation for his charity foundation.

The showdown featured in MrBeast 's video Beat LeBron, Win $100,000 , released Saturday and filmed in Akron , Ohio , during James ' offseason before he joined the 76ers in free agency. The challenge put him under pressure in front of young cancer survivors.

And James was quick to acknowledge that he does not possess the shooting reputation of Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry but still gave it his best go in order to raise cash for the LeBron James Family Foundation .

“I’m no Steph Curry, but I can make a couple of shots,” LeBron joked before stepping in for the one-minute competition whilst MrBeast missed his practice attempt, giving the professional basketballer confidence to take him on.

The children watching were also firmly behind the four-time NBA champion, with some of Donaldson 's own friends suggesting the YouTuber had little chance of winning and the contest proved much closer than expected.

James started well, but MrBeast recovered from a slow opening to draw level midway through the minute as both competitors continued shooting as the clock wound down, with the professional athlete eventually claiming a narrow 6-5 victory to secure $100,000 for foundation and provided one of the standout moments in a wider charity initiative.

The shootout was filmed as part of MrBeast 's July video, I Helped 100 Kids Fight Cancer , which brought together celebrities, athletes and organizations to create experiences for young patients and the event also included a film premiere with Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson , a meeting with K-pop group Stray Kids and a day with the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The 76ers demonstrated their depth in quality as the team 40 percent from three-point range and overcame Charlotte 's 15-of-23 performance at the free-throw line to claim a sixth win of the season and to maintain their lead atop the Eastern Conference .

articles.standfirst: Lakers and Raptors test their credentials this Sunday; Dončić against the Canadian defensive block
articles.summary: Lakers and Raptors test their credentials this Sunday; Dončić against the Canadian defensive block
articles.body:
The start of the NBA season leaves a matchup with plenty to unpack: the Los Angeles Lakers host the Toronto Raptors at Crypto.com Arena, in a clash between two teams that arrive with winning records and their sights set on establishing themselves as contenders in their respective conferences.

Lakers vs Raptors Schedule and Where to Watch Live

The matchup is scheduled for this Sunday, November 1, 2026, with tip-off at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time (8:00 p.m. Central Time and 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time). The venue will be Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, with a capacity of 20,000 fans.

In the United States, local broadcast coverage is handled by Spectrum Sports Net, with the streaming option available through Spectrum Sports Net +, the Lakers’ regional broadcasts as the home team. At the league-wide rights level, you can watch it on Amazon Prime Video and with NBA League Pass.

The context in the table: How are the Lakers and Raptors coming into today's game?

Both teams come in with the same efficiency: a 4-2 record for the Lakers and 3-2 for the Raptors, leaving both with winning percentages of .667 and .600, respectively.

The Los Angeles team leads the Pacific Division and sits in fifth place in the Western Conference, just one and a half games out of first. Toronto, meanwhile, is third in the Atlantic Division and fourth in the Eastern Conference, also one and a half games behind the lead.

In the overall league standings, the Lakers are in ninth place and the Raptors in fourteenth, separated by a handful of spots in a table that is still very tight after barely half a dozen games.

A defensive statistic stands out: Toronto is among the teams that have allowed the fewest points in the entire league, with 531 points against in five games, an identical figure to that of Memphis, the overall leader.

That solidity at the back will be their best argument in a scenario where the Lakers average a high-powered offense: 711 points scored in six games.

The Lakers come in on a roll. They have won four of their last five, including a solid 103-87 victory over the Clippers in their most recent visit and significant wins over Golden State and Utah.

The only stumble was a high-scoring loss to Portland, 129-136, a game where the defense fell short. That combination—overflowing offense but leaks at the back—defines the Los Angeles team in this opening stretch.

Toronto comes in with three wins in their last four, highlighted by two blowouts: 135-92 over Chicago and 129-99 over Orlando, along with a hard-fought win on the road against Washington.

Their only stumble came in Minnesota, where they fell 94-117, the only game in which their offense went completely cold. The Canadian pattern is clear: when they tighten up on defense, they crush; when they’re taken out of their rhythm, they suffer.

articles.title: Michael Jordan's challenging condition to appear on a podcast: “All he wants to do is gamble”
articles.standfirst: Stephen Jackson and Matt Barnes are determined to interview the Bulls legend
articles.summary: Stephen Jackson and Matt Barnes are determined to interview the Bulls legend
articles.body:
M ichael Jordan 's competitive instincts have never disappeared since his retirement from basketball, and they are now proving an unexpected obstacle for two former NBA players hoping to secure one of the biggest interviews in sports.

Stephen Jackson and Matt Barnes have welcomed numerous prominent athletes and entertainers onto their All the Smoke podcast, but the six-time NBA champion remains one of the most elusive names on their guest list.

During a recent conversation with rapper Jeezy , Jackson revealed that he has repeatedly approached Jordan about appearing on the show, only to receive invitations to compete against him on the golf course instead.

"I text him about the show and he'll text back, 'Bring your sorry a** to the golf course and bring your money,'" Jackson explained.

The response amused Jeezy , who had suggested Jordan as his ideal podcast guest after revealing that he recently encountered the former Chicago Bulls star in Portugal.

"All he wants to do is gamble," Jeezy joked, prompting Jackson to agree: "He just wants to take something from you."

Despite the playful exchanges, Jackson remains determined to arrange an appearance from Jordan , whose public interviews have become increasingly rare since his playing career ended.

Jackson 's longstanding relationship with Jordan , developed partly through his association with Jordan Brand, has given him direct access to the basketball icon.

However, that personal connection hasn't been enough to convince Jordan to participate in an extended conversation about his career, experiences and life away from the NBA.

Jeezy believes such an interview would offer fans a perspective they rarely receive from someone whose extraordinary achievements have already been extensively documented.

"You guys are the culture, like the culture needs to hear from him," Jeezy said.

"We just see Jordan, but we don't really know Jordan. Him coming here would give people a chance just to know him. He's a dope dude, man. Jordan's solid."

Rather than abandoning the idea, Jackson and Barnes discussed taking their recording equipment directly onto the golf course, where Jordan would presumably feel more comfortable.

"I told him we'll come anywhere, bro," Jackson said, emphasizing how far the hosts are prepared to go to secure the interview.

Absence from NBA television adds to interest

Jordan 's limited media appearances have made the prospect of a full podcast conversation particularly appealing, especially after his brief involvement with NBC's basketball coverage disappointed some viewers.

His MJ: Insights to Excellence segments during the 2025-26 season were drawn from a prerecorded interview with Mike Tirico , rather than regular appearances discussing current NBA developments.

NBC has since confirmed that Jordan isn't expected to return in the same capacity this season, meaning opportunities to hear directly from the five-time NBA MVP remain limited.

Jordan 's enthusiasm for competitive golf has been documented for decades, including stories from Charles Barkley about lengthy rounds and his determination to win regardless of the stakes.

Jackson has suggested that even an exhausting day on the course would be worthwhile if it finally persuaded Jordan to sit down for an interview.

Whether that arrangement ever materializes remains uncertain, but the podcast hosts appear prepared to meet Jordan on his own terms, even if doing so comes at a considerable financial cost.

articles.title: Should the Trail Blazers be worried about Ja Morant's latest injury?
articles.standfirst: The player was beginning to establish a role alongside the team's other backcourt options
articles.summary: The player was beginning to establish a role alongside the team's other backcourt options
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers have reasons to be encouraged by their early-season start, but Ja Morant's latest injury presents an immediate test for a team hoping to turn its backcourt talent into sustained success. Morant will miss four weeks after suffering a Grade 2 strain of his left hamstring, the Trail Blazers announced.

The injury occurred Thursday night against the Memphis Grizzlies , the team that traded the guard to Portland in the offseason. Morant scored 14 points in 23 minutes before the injury overshadowed a game in which the Trail Blazers suffered their first loss of the season.

The timing is frustrating for Portland. Morant had shown encouraging signs in his first four games with the franchise, averaging 15.8 points and 5.5 assists while shooting 54.2% from the field and 42.9% from 3-point range.

Those numbers suggested he was finding his footing in a new setting and beginning to establish a role alongside the team's other backcourt options. Now, the Trail Blazers must adjust without him for at least the next month. Should Portland be concerned? Yes, particularly about Morant's availability over the long term, rather than the immediate impact of a four-week absence.

A Grade 2 hamstring strain is a significant setback, and the re-evaluation timeline does not guarantee Morant will be ready to return immediately afterward. The team will have to manage his recovery carefully, especially given his history of injuries and the limited number of games he played last season.

Morant's injury history raises the stakes

The latest setback is concerning because it adds another chapter to a series of injury interruptions in Morant's recent seasons . The 27-year-old appeared in just 20 games during the 2025-26 campaign because of an elbow sprain, limiting his opportunity to build rhythm and remain consistently available.

Now, a hamstring injury threatens to disrupt another season before it has fully developed. Missing four weeks can make it difficult to maintain conditioning and continuity. For a guard whose game depends heavily on acceleration, changes of direction and attacking defenders off the dribble, hamstring health is especially important. Portland will have to be cautious about bringing Morant back before he is ready, even if the team is eager to restore its full rotation.

The distinction between a four-week re-evaluation and a firm return date matters. The former means the Trail Blazers will assess his progress at that point; it does not establish that he will immediately resume playing. His recovery, response to rehabilitation and ability to handle basketball activity will determine the next step. Portland should resist the temptation to treat the announced timeline as a deadline.

The bigger concern is availability, not talent

Morant's ability to influence a game is not the central issue. His strong start in Portland showed that he can still be an efficient scorer while contributing as a playmaker. The concern is whether he can remain healthy enough to build on those flashes and develop consistent chemistry with his new teammates.

That question carries particular weight after a season in which he played only 20 games. Another extended absence would mean more missed opportunities to learn the offense, establish reliable rotations and develop the kind of continuity that teams need as the season progresses. It also creates uncertainty for Portland's long-term planning.

A talented backcourt can give a team a high ceiling, but the potential of that group depends on its key players being available together. Every extended absence makes it harder to evaluate how effective the lineup can be when fully healthy.

Still, it would be premature to draw sweeping conclusions from this injury alone. A hamstring strain does not automatically mean Morant will continue to experience recurring problems, and his recovery will provide a clearer indication of how quickly he can return to form.

The Trail Blazers' immediate priority should be protecting Morant's recovery while keeping the team competitive. His four-week re-evaluation will be an important checkpoint, but the organization should focus on his readiness rather than rushing to meet a particular date.

articles.title: Where to watch Philadelphia 76ers vs Chicago Bulls and what time does this Monday's game start?
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia, leaders of the East, host the free-falling Bulls at the Wells Fargo Center
articles.summary: Philadelphia, leaders of the East, host the free-falling Bulls at the Wells Fargo Center
articles.body:
There are games in which the schedule seems like a whim, and this is one of them. The Philadelphia 76ers, owners of the best start in the Eastern Conference, open the doors of the Wells Fargo Center to a Chicago Bulls team that can't find its footing.

The contrast could not be sharper: Philadelphia arrives looking every bit a contender, while Chicago tries to stop a bleeding that already has it at the bottom of the league.

Where to watch the Sixers vs Bulls game and what time does it start?

The game will be played this Monday, November 2, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. Eastern Time (Central European Time), at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, a venue with a capacity of 20,478 fans.

For the U.S. audience, the local broadcast of the game depends on each team's market: in Philadelphia it will be on NBC Sports Philadelphia and, in Chicago, it can be watched on Chicago Sports Network.

Overall, the game between the Sixers and the Bulls will be broadcast with NBA League Pass as a complementary streaming option.

Philadelphia 76ers, with a leader's identity

The 76ers lead the Eastern Conference with a 6-1 record in seven games played, the best winning record in the East and one of the three best in the entire league. In the overall standings, they occupy third place among the 30 franchises.

Their recent streak supports the optimism. Philadelphia is coming off a run of significant wins: they won at the home of the New York Knicks, defeated Cleveland and Milwaukee at the Wells Fargo Center, and recently recorded two straight road victories against Indiana and Charlotte.

The only stumble in that stretch was a home loss to Detroit, a reminder that the only opponent to have beaten them is also battling at the top.

The team leading this roster brings together a rare mix of veteran experience and young talent: Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey as the backbone, with Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, and shooting guard Anfernee Simons providing offensive firepower, along with young Bahamian point guard VJ Edgecombe, just 21 years old.

It is a rotation capable of scoring in waves, something a defensively fragile opponent should fear.

Chicago Bulls, looking to stop the slide

The Bulls' outlook is the opposite. With a 1-5 record, Chicago sinks to 26th place in the overall standings and sits fourth in the Central Division, ahead of only Milwaukee. Their point differential is among the most worrying in the East, a symptom of a team that gives up too much: 776 points allowed in six games.

Their recent run is nightmarish. After being blown out in Toronto, they earned their only win of the season in Milwaukee, but since then they have piled up three straight losses: at home against Washington (120-124), a rout in Boston, and another painful setback against the Knicks. The pattern is clear: when Chicago scores, it also allows scoring without restraint.

The roster, though, has some interesting young pieces. Australian point guard Josh Giddey is the creative engine, with shooter Buddy Hield, shooting guard Norman Powell, playmaker Tre Jones, and promising Lithuanian forward Matas Buzelis rounding out a core that points more to the future than the present.

Inside, Nic Claxton and Zach Collins carry the responsibility in the paint, precisely the area where Embiid can do damage.

Implications in the Eastern Conference standings

For the 76ers, a win would solidify their lead in the East and keep them tied in victories with the league’s best in this early stretch. They also sit atop the Atlantic Division, ahead of Boston. It is not a game in which they can afford to relax, but it is one in which everything points to them needing to capitalize.

For the Bulls, each loss carries double weight in an increasingly crowded lower tier. They share the bottom of the East with Milwaukee, and only Brooklyn and, overall, Sacramento remain below them. Picking up points in Philadelphia would be almost a feat, but avoiding another blowout would already be a first step toward stopping the spiral.

76ers vs Bulls Prediction

The numbers and the form point in one direction only. Philadelphia is playing at home, comes in on a roll, has the decisive advantage in the paint, and faces an opponent that gives up too easily.

The logical outcome is a clear victory for the 76ers; the only real question is whether Chicago can keep the score competitive or if it turns into another long night for a franchise urgently seeking its second bit of joy of the season.

articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers host the Miami Heat this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, with the two franchises heading in opposite directions at the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season.

While the Lakers settle in among the best in the West, the Florida team arrives mired in the lower reaches of the Eastern Conference. It’s the classic clash between a team brimming with confidence and another desperate to stop the bleeding.

The state of affairs: This is how the Lakers and Miami arrive for today's game

The Lakers are fourth in the Western Conference with a record of 5 wins and 2 losses, and they lead the Pacific Division ahead of the Golden State Warriors.

Their offense has been one of the most prolific at the start: 842 points scored in seven games, the highest total in their entire conference. At home they have been especially formidable, and they are coming off a packed schedule that they have managed to capitalize on.

Miami, meanwhile, is going through a difficult stretch. The Heat are last in the Southeast Division and sit 19th overall with just 2 wins and 4 losses.

Their -19 point differential reflects a team that gives up too much and still hasn't found consistency. They are also hosting an opponent that has scored 125 or more points in five of its last six games.

The Lakers' recent stretch speaks for itself. They have piled up five wins in their last six games, with only one stumble along the way:

Los Angeles Lakers 127 - 105 Golden State Warriors

Los Angeles Lakers 125 - 117 Los Angeles Clippers

Los Angeles Lakers 132 - 123 Utah Jazz

Los Angeles Lakers 129 - 136 Portland Trail Blazers

Los Angeles Lakers 103 - 87 Los Angeles Clippers

Los Angeles Lakers 95 - 112 Golden State Warriors

Los Angeles Lakers 131 - 125 Toronto Raptors

That 131-125 result against Toronto was just yesterday, November 1, so the home team enters this matchup with minimal rest but momentum on its side.

Miami, on the other hand, comes in battered. Their most recent run shows four defeats and only one bright spot:

Miami Heat 106 - 131 Minnesota Timberwolves

Miami Heat 111 - 128 Detroit Pistons

Miami Heat 110 - 115 Charlotte Hornets

Miami Heat 109 - 113 Dallas Mavericks

Miami Heat 129 - 117 Atlanta Hawks

Miami Heat 145 - 125 Indiana Pacers

The victory in Atlanta, with 129 points, showed that the firepower is there when the team loosens up. The problem has been the defense: in three of those four losses, it allowed 113 points or more.

Lineups for Lakers vs Heat: star power on both sides

The biggest appeal lies in the individual talent. The Lakers rely on Luka Dončić, the 27-year-old Slovenian who leads the Los Angeles offense, accompanied by a quality core with Austin Reaves and Collin Sexton on the perimeter.

In theory, the arrival of players like Walker Kessler and the veteran presence of Kevon Looney give the team size and rebounding, while Jarred Vanderbilt and Matisse Thybulle provide the defensive energy that often makes the difference in physical matchups.

On Miami’s side, the focus is on Giannis Antetokounmpo, the 31-year-old Greek star who leads the Heat’s project, supported by interior pillar Bam Adebayo. They are joined by the scoring experience of Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. from the perimeter, as well as the aggressiveness of Bobby Portis and Andrew Wiggins at the forward positions.

It is a roster with name recognition and stature; what it lacks is translating that talent into defensive consistency. The matchup between Adebayo and the Los Angeles frontcourt, added to the battle between Dončić and Antetokounmpo as the engines of their respective offenses, defines much of what can happen on the hardwood.

For the Lakers, every win is gold in a tightly packed West: the leading Memphis Grizzlies and the Houston Rockets are setting a fierce pace, and the Angelenos are 1.5 games out of the top spot in the conference.

articles.title: The $203.6 million Stephen Curry will earn next year sets him apart from LeBron James following his latest decision
articles.standfirst: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers move gives Stephen Curry an even bigger financial advantage
articles.summary: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers move gives Stephen Curry an even bigger financial advantage
articles.body:
Stephen Curry’s projected $203.6 million haul for the coming year has created a financial gap that even LeBron James can’t match.

Forbes’ 2026 list of the NBA’s highest-paid players places the Golden State Warriors guard first for a second consecutive year, with almost $100 million separating him from runner-up Kevin Durant.

His latest financial achievement further demonstrates how Curry has built an empire beyond his basketball career.

The 38-year-old is expected to collect $62.6 million from basketball and another $141 million through endorsements and business interests. His off-court income is particularly impressive, representing a substantial rise from the $100 million he reportedly generated away from basketball last year.

Curry’s split with Under Armour in 2025 left him without a major footwear partner for a period, but he has since agreed to a 10-year, $400 million partnership with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning.

The agreement includes a signature shoe range expected to arrive early next year. Forbes says Curry is the first active NBA player projected to pass $200 million in a 12-month period. Only Floyd Mayweather, Cristiano Ronaldo and Jon Rahm have previously reached that level among athletes tracked by the publication.

LeBron’s contract decision widens Curry’s financial advantage

Durant ranks second with an estimated $104.9 million, followed by Giannis Antetokounmpo at $103.5 million. LeBron , meanwhile, has fallen to fourth at $93.9 million after 11 consecutive seasons leading the NBA earnings list.

His commercial income remains formidable at an estimated $90 million. However, his decision to join the Philadelphia 76ers on a veteran-minimum deal worth $3.9 million has dramatically reduced his basketball earnings.

That contract leaves James with a projected total that's less than half of Curry's earnings, highlighting the enormous difference between the two superstars. Despite the drop in his ranking, LeBron remains one of the most commercially successful athletes in the world, with endorsements and business ventures continuing to generate substantial revenue.

Anthony Edwards ($87.9 million) and Jayson Tatum ($86.5 million) occupy fifth and sixth, while Jimmy Butler and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander are tied at $70.8 million. Devin Booker and Joel Embiid complete the top ten.

The list’s wider picture is just as notable. Its ten players are projected to earn $958 million combined, including $469 million from commercial ventures and endorsements. That off-court figure highlights the growing commercial influence of NBA superstars and the value major brands place on their partnerships.

Golden State also has a fresh on-court storyline. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 points and added six assists in the Warriors' 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers. His performance made him the first Warriors rookie to score at least 35 points in a game since Curry recorded 42 in November 2010.

Lendeborg's emergence offers another reason for optimism in Golden State, particularly as the franchise navigates injuries and absences among established players. Meanwhile, Curry continues to dominate headlines through his achievements both on and off the court.

articles.title: Choked up and tearful: Russell Westbrook’s emotional reaction to Thunder’s ultimate honor
articles.standfirst: The former MVP gets emotional as Oklahoma City prepares to immortalize his remarkable contribution to the franchise
articles.summary: The former MVP gets emotional as Oklahoma City prepares to immortalize his remarkable contribution to the franchise
articles.body:
Russell Westbrook’s place in Oklahoma City basketball history is about to receive a permanent tribute. The Thunder have announced that they’ll retire his iconic No. 0 jersey on February 7, when they host the New York Knicks at Paycom Center.

The recognition carries meaning far beyond a number being lifted into the rafters for a player whose identity became closely tied to the franchise.

Westbrook’s response made that clear.

“It’s amazing; it’s a true blessing,” Westbrook said. “Quite frankly, it's not just for me, my family — my kids, wife, my mom, my brother-in-law, the entire city. Being able to grow up not even imagining you'd be able to be a professional athlete, needless to say, be in the NBA.

“But to be able to get your jersey retired, it creates a legacy; it creates a sense of all the work, time, effort, and energy you put into the game. I'm just truly grateful for that honor. I look forward to that night.”

A legacy built over 11 seasons

The Thunder selected Westbrook fourth overall in the 2008 NBA Draft, shortly before the franchise relocated from Seattle to Oklahoma City. He spent his first 11 NBA seasons with the organization, becoming one of its most recognizable figures and helping establish its identity.

During that period, Oklahoma City reached the Western Conference finals four times and advanced to the NBA Finals in 2012. Westbrook played a central role in the team's rise, developing into one of the league's most explosive and accomplished guards.

His individual achievements were equally impressive. He won the NBA Most Valuable Player award in 2016-17 after becoming the first player since Oscar Robertson to average a triple-double across an entire season.

He subsequently repeated that remarkable statistical achievement in two consecutive campaigns. Westbrook also captured two scoring titles and led the league in assists three times.

His numbers in Oklahoma City further explain why the franchise considers him worthy of its highest recognition. Westbrook finished his Thunder career with 18,859 points, 6,897 assists, 5,760 rebounds and 1,442 steals. He also recorded 138 triple-doubles in a Thunder uniform, establishing a remarkable franchise benchmark.

General manager Sam Presti praised Westbrook's contributions both on and off the basketball court.

“Many players made an impact, but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook was built both on the court and in the community,” Presti said.

“His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own, and his number will be raised to the rafters in Oklahoma City forever.”

Westbrook will become only the second player to have his number retired specifically for his contributions to the Oklahoma City Thunder, joining Nick Collison.

Although several other numbers hang in the rafters from the franchise's Seattle SuperSonics history, Westbrook's recognition represents an important chapter in Oklahoma City's own basketball story.

articles.title: Dennis Rodman, NBA legend: “Madonna offered me $20 million to get her pregnant when she was ovulating”
articles.standfirst: The former player recalled the unexpected call he received from the Queen of Pop and the private jet ride he says he took to meet her.
articles.summary: The former player recalled the unexpected call he received from the Queen of Pop and the private jet ride he says he took to meet her.
articles.body:
Everyone has their own way of imagining and planning their future, but Madonna apparently knew exactly what she wanted at the time . At least, that's how Dennis Rodman remembers it. The former NBA star claims the singer once offered him $20 million to get her pregnant .

Dennis Rodman received a call from Madonna while playing in Las Vegas

Rodman recalled that he was in Las Vegas when someone told him Madonna wanted to speak with him . His first reaction was to assume someone was playing a prank on him, but once he realized the call was genuine, he decided to answer.

On the other end of the line was the singer, who, according to Rodman, got straight to the point: she told him she was ovulating . The former basketball player admitted that he didn't immediately understand exactly what she meant, but he soon figured out why she was calling. His response was quick: he would be with her in five hours.

To make that happen, he left the dice on the table, asked someone to hold his spot and headed straight for the airport. According to his account, Madonna had sent a private jet to fly him from Las Vegas to New York, where she was waiting for him .

But the story didn't end with that trip. During the conversation, Rodman was also asked whether Madonna had later wanted to know if he had managed to get her pregnant. The former NBA star said yes, although he didn't share any further details.

Dennis Rodman and Madonna dated in 1990

Their story didn't come out of nowhere. Dennis Rodman and Madonna were romantically involved in 1990, when both were making headlines for very different reasons .

He was beginning to establish himself as a force in the NBA, thanks to his extraordinary defensive skills and dominance on the boards. She, meanwhile, was experiencing one of the biggest periods of her career and continuing to cement her status as one of pop music's biggest stars.

Although they came from completely different worlds, both had larger-than-life personalities that made them hard to ignore.

articles.title: Lakers fan cam moment sparks debate over parenting after dad covers daughter
articles.standfirst: The clip's reception illustrated how even a small gesture at an NBA game can become a talking point once it reaches social media
articles.summary: The clip's reception illustrated how even a small gesture at an NBA game can become a talking point once it reaches social media
articles.body:
A seemingly ordinary moment during a Los Angeles Lakers game at Crypto.com Arena has sparked a debate online about parenting, privacy and how quickly a viral clip can turn into a discussion about family values. A cameraman focused on a man and his daughters in the stands, putting the family on the arena's big screen.

But when the father noticed that one of his daughters' outfits appeared to be slipping out of place, he reacted quickly, moving his hand in front of her to cover the exposed area. The brief interaction caught the attention of viewers, with some praising the father for noticing the situation and responding immediately to help his daughter avoid an uncomfortable moment in front of a packed arena.

Others, however, questioned why the family had not addressed the clothing issue before attending the game, turning a lighthearted moment into a broader argument about parental responsibility and personal choice. The clip's reception illustrated how even a small, spontaneous gesture at an NBA game can become a talking point once it reaches social media.

'Dad of the year'? Fans praise the father's instincts

For many viewers, the father's reaction was exactly what a parent should do: notice a potential wardrobe malfunction and step in before the situation became more embarrassing for his daughter. One online commenter highlighted the importance of being attentive to children's comfort, writing: "Parenting is often about noticing the little things before they become uncomfortable moments for your children. That quick reaction says a lot."

The sentiment resonated with people who saw the incident as an example of a parent looking out for his children without making a scene. Rather than waiting for his daughter to notice the problem herself or allowing the moment to become more awkward, the father appeared to respond instinctively. His quick movement was enough to prompt playful praise from viewers, with some calling him a "Dad of the year" candidate.

The setting also played a role in the reaction. NBA games regularly feature fan cams and crowd shots, turning spectators into part of the entertainment. While these moments can be fun, they can also put fans in front of thousands of people, as well as viewers watching at home and online. For supporters of the father, his response showed an awareness that an unexpected camera appearance can create an uncomfortable situation, particularly when a wardrobe issue is involved.

Critics question the family's clothing choices

Not everyone interpreted the clip as a straightforward parenting success story. Some commenters shifted the discussion toward the daughter's outfit, arguing that the father should have addressed the issue before the family arrived at the arena. "So why didn't he ask her to dress appropriately in the first place?" one user asked.

Another commenter wrote, "Teach them how to dress instead, maybe?" A third questioned the apparent contradiction between allowing someone to wear an outfit and then trying to cover it when the camera appeared: "Why is he hiding them now when he himself gave them permission to wear that in public?"

These reactions moved the conversation away from the father's quick reflexes and toward a familiar debate about clothing, parental guidance and individual autonomy. Critics suggested that preventing an embarrassing situation begins before it happens. Others viewed the father's reaction as a reasonable response to an unexpected moment, regardless of what his daughter had chosen to wear.

The debate also raises questions about where parental responsibility ends and personal choice begins. Depending on the daughters' ages, the family's approach to clothing may involve different considerations, but the clip alone does not establish what conversations took place before the game or how the daughter felt about the incident.

articles.title: Sip of controversy: LeBron James risks NBA penalty after drinking fan’s beverage mid-game
articles.standfirst: Now the NBA could decide whether the viral wine sip deserves a punishment.
articles.summary: Now the NBA could decide whether the viral wine sip deserves a punishment.
articles.body:
During Monday night’s game between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Chicago Bulls at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 2 , LeBron James provided one of the evening’s most memorable and unusual moments by interacting with a fan.

Behind one of the baskets, the veteran grabbed a fan’s cup and took a sip. According to ESPN’s Kris Rhim , the season-ticket holder — identified as Troy Clemens — offered LeBron some of his wine during the game.

Stadium cameras captured the scene, which quickly went viral on social media and sparked speculation about whether the NBA might take disciplinary action.

Will LeBron James be fined for drinking wine during the game?

This is not the first time LeBron has had an unusual interaction with fans during a game. In 2017 , during the Cleveland Cavaliers’ playoff series against the Toronto Raptors , he playfully pretended to drink a beer courtside. The league took no action against him.

Nor would it be the first time a 76ers player has been involved in a similar situation. In 2019 , then-Philadelphia forward Mike Scott went viral when he drank from a fan’s cup during a game against the Milwaukee Bucks . Scott jumped into the stands, took the cup, sipped from it, and returned to the court. The NBA reviewed the incident but decided against a fine, and the 76ers imposed no internal discipline either.

While the league may review LeBron’s interaction with the fan , it appears unlikely that the 41-year-old will receive a financial penalty for a moment that quickly became one of the most talked-about highlights of the night.

articles.title: Unbelievable: the Pacers played with only six players against the Hawks!
articles.standfirst: Injuries are ravaging the start of the NBA regular season
articles.summary: Injuries are ravaging the start of the NBA regular season
articles.body:
It is a fact that injuries are changing the NBA landscape at the start of the season. In the West , for example, although the Thunder are holding up, the three long-term injuries to three of their starters, two for the entire season , leave them with fewer chances of fighting for the title. Houston , for example, has emerged as the main alternative to the Spurs in that conference. And we are only two weeks in.

But it hasn’t only been the Thunder . There are many teams that are already missing many of their players, even league stars . And the Indiana Pacers are one of the hardest hit, so much so that they have been involved in something unprecedented in the NBA at this point in the schedule.

And, between injuries and rest—often mandatory— Rick Carlisle had only six players available to face the Atlanta Hawks in Indiana . In more than 80 years of history, only one similar case is remembered this early: the Lakers in 1948 , with five players in their third game of the season.

It is not the first time that a team has played with six players , of course. There have been several cases in recent years, but never so close to the start of the season . It is a case more typically reserved for the period near the end of the regular season and the start of the Playoffs.

Even so, the Indiana players made the Georgia team suffer, 104-108, but of course they ended the game exhausted. The player who spent the least time on the court was Quenton Jackson , 35 minutes, and Kobe Brown , who came off the bench, played 38.

The Pacers' injury list is immense: Tyrese Haliburton (hamstrings), Pascal Siakam (rest), Johnny Furphy (knee), T.J. McConnell (hamstrings), Larry Nance Jr. (illness), Andrew Nembhard (cervical area), Aaron Nesmith (hamstrings), Ben Sheppard (knee), Obi Toppin (lumbar sprain) and Ivica Zubac (ankle). Kelly Oubre Jr. was a last-minute scratch due to a knee contusion.

Put another way: the list of absences adds up to nearly 200 million in salaries , while the six players who took the court barely reach 15 million . The Pacers had to face this game with three players on two-way contracts, that is, whose careers are spent in the G League and sometimes in the NBA: Braden Smith, Jalen Slawson and Kobe Brown.

Tonight marks the first time the Pacers have played an NBA game with six players since November 20, 2004. That was the night after the " Malice at the Palace ," the monumental brawl between the Pacers and the Pistons that ended with numerous ejections and suspensions.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball, faster than anyone in the race for three-pointers in the NBA
articles.standfirst: He is the player who reaches 1,000 three-pointers in the fewest games played
articles.summary: He is the player who reaches 1,000 three-pointers in the fewest games played
articles.body:
When on January 7, 2015, Stephen Curry reached 1,000 three-pointers in his 369th game, it was said to be a record that would last a long time. And it did, although only for seven years, when Buddy Hield , on February 28, 2021 , needed only 350 games to reach the milestone. Now, that mark set by Hield has been completely shattered.

In fact, the previous record, 343 games by Duncan Robinson since March 17, 2024, has been shattered by the feat that LaMelo Ball has just achieved in a game in which he reached his season-high scoring mark of 34, while leading the Timberwolves to their fifth win of the season against the Milwaukee Bucks, 112-100.

LaMelo , who had been listed as doubtful due to a blow to the wrist, made six three-pointers in the game. The third goes straight into the history books because it is the 1,000th of his career . The Wolves player brings the number of games needed to achieve it down to 311 , lowering the previous mark set by Robinson by 32. The Wolves player is the fastest player to have amassed those 1,000 three-pointers in NBA history.

Ball has emerged as a very reliable shooter despite having shown some problems with that facet at different stages of his career. At 25 years old he has managed to incorporate the three-point shot as a fundamental weapon. Now, though not as an obsession, it remains to be seen whether he is capable of threatening Stephen Curry's throne as the NBA's top three-point shooter. The Warriors star has 4,270 and counting. That's saying a lot.

articles.body:
There are players who transcend history, and one of them is Russell Westbrook . His game can be debated, whether he was ever a player capable of making a team champion (he did reach the Finals, in 2012), or whether he often played to pad his statistics. But no one can doubt the impact this point guard had on the teams he played for , especially the Thunder , who on February 7 will pay him the highest tribute possible.

Oklahoma announced it this Tuesday: on that day, coinciding with the visit of the champion Knicks , his jersey with the unmistakable number 0 will go straight up to the rafters of the Paycom Center to stand there as the second retired number in the franchise since it moved from Seattle, after the 4 of Nick Collison.

Days after that relocation, Russell Westbrook was selected with the No. 4 pick in the Draft, the team's first pick as the Thunder . He played 11 of the 18 seasons he has spent in the NBA there. Alongside Kevin Durant , who had been there a year earlier when they were still playing in Seattle , James Harden , who arrived in 2009, and Serge Ibaka , selected in the same Draft as the point guard, they managed to reach the 2012 Finals, losing to the Miami Heat, 4-1.

Durant's departure in 2016 only served to enhance Westbrook 's stature, and the following year he became the first player to average a triple-double for the season (31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists) since Oscar Robertson in 1962 , and he was named MVP . Then, Westbrook added to the feat with another two more triple-double seasons , the last with the Thunder .

After Oklahoma , in Westbrook 's career, there were the Houston Rockets, the Washington Wizards, the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Clippers, the Denver Nuggets and the Sacramento Kings , until his retirement at the end of last season.

Sam Presti, executive vice president and general manager of the Thunder, was responsible for announcing the ceremony: " Many players make an impact, but only great players leave a legacy . Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," Presti said in a statement. " His mindset was relentless and his commitment, profound. For all these reasons, the people of Oklahoma consider him one of their own, and his number will be raised to the rafters in Oklahoma City forever ".

articles.title: Michael Wilbon steps away from ESPN indefinitely due to health issues: “I have to listen”
articles.standfirst: The longtime host of Pardon the Interruption explained that he is dealing with several health issues and decided to take some time off to recover. At 67, he clarified that this is not a retirement.
articles.summary: The longtime host of Pardon the Interruption explained that he is dealing with several health issues and decided to take some time off to recover. At 67, he clarified that this is not a retirement.
articles.body:
Michael Wilbon announced this Monday that he will take an indefinite leave from ESPN and ABC due to several health issues that have worsened over the past few months. The 67-year-old journalist will temporarily step away from both Pardon the Interruption and his duties related to NBA coverage.

The decision comes after Wilbon was absent for a week from the program he hosts alongside Tony Kornheiser. In a conversation with his colleague, he acknowledged that he was “more than exhausted” and that he had been dealing with that situation for some time. He also explained that diabetes is part of the problems he is facing, although it is not the only reason for his current condition.

Wilbon rules out this being a complete retirement.

The journalist wanted to make it clear that his absence does not mean the end of his career. In a message posted on social media, he described his decision as a “trip to the injured list” and expressed his hope that it would not be too prolonged. “This is not a retirement,” he said while explaining his leave from PTI and his responsibilities with the NBA.

Wilbon also acknowledged that he should have listened earlier to doctors and the people around him, including Kornheiser, who had warned of worrying signs in recent years. According to him, the problems he is going through are exclusively health-related and are not connected to alcohol or gambling.

The absence comes just days after the 25th anniversary of Pardon the Interruption, one of ESPN’s most recognizable programs. Wilbon and Kornheiser began hosting it in 2001 and have kept the format together for a quarter of a century.

What a wild and incredible 25 years it has been! We are beyond grateful to all our loyal Knuckleheads. Join us on this journey through PTI memories...

During his appearance on Kornheiser's podcast, Wilbon explained that the symptoms had reached a point where he could no longer ignore them. “I have to listen”, he said, referring to the signs that are forcing him to stop and focus on his recovery.

ESPN publicly expressed its support for the journalist and said it hopes to welcome him back when he is ready to return. In the meantime, the network will rely on guest hosts to cover his absence on PTI, while other analysts will take over some of his NBA-related duties.

Wilbon's last appearance on Pardon the Interruption took place on October 26. For now, there is no set date for his return . The journalist himself admitted that he does not know exactly how long this period will last, although his goal is to recover and return to share the program with Kornheiser.

articles.title: There will be no NBA so that the United States can go vote
articles.standfirst: The midterm elections are being held
articles.summary: The midterm elections are being held
articles.body:
The NBA will not schedule games in the early hours from Tuesday to Wednesday due to the United States midterm election day , and to encourage fans and the league community to vote.

Americans are called to renew the entire House of Representatives and one third of the Senate, as well as elect state and local offices.

The competition leaves election day free for the fourth time in the last five years. The initiative began in 2022 and continued in 2023 and 2024 , before the league scheduled games on that date in 2025 .

The NBA announced the reinstatement of this measure when unveiling the 2026-2027 season schedule and explained that it seeks to encourage its community to plan their vote.

All 30 teams had games scheduled this Monday, and the competition will resume on Wednesday, November 4, with 14 matchups.

articles.title: An out-of-this-world Doncic: "He's a supernova, with him we're in a spaceship"
articles.standfirst: The NBA falls at the feet of the Slovenian genius, who is revered by rivals and teammates alike: "When he is on the court, we move at the speed of light"
articles.summary: The NBA falls at the feet of the Slovenian genius, who is revered by rivals and teammates alike: "When he is on the court, we move at the speed of light"
articles.body:
There are players who dominate a game and others who make it seem like they’re playing a different sport . Luka Doncic belongs to the latter. His performance against the Miami Heat, with 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds , was yet another masterclass from a player who has turned the extraordinary into routine and who, at 27 years old, seems to have no ceiling. The NBA bows at his feet .

His is starting to escape any statistical logic. Five consecutive games scoring at least 37 points, four of them surpassing 40 , and an outrageous ease in tearing apart any defense put in front of him. Doncic scores, assists, rebounds and decides . He does it in every possible way and with a naturalness that turns every night into a spectacle. Not even the records seem to be on his level.

At the start of this season, with the Lakers off to a flying start (6-2), his MVP candidacy is already a reality . But beyond the numbers and the wins, there is something that better than anything else defines the magnitude of the Slovenian: the admiration he inspires among those who share a locker room with him and, above all, among those who suffer through his masterclasses from the other side of the court. Teammates, rivals, and coaches are left without words in the face of a player from another planet .

Luka no longer just dazzles: he inspires reverence

Because when someone like Giannis Antetokounmpo , one of the NBA's great dominators, says that Doncic is "one of the best scorers ever to play this sport, if not the best" , words are hardly necessary. His coach, JJ Redick , speaks of a "supernova"; his teammates watch his feats in disbelief and his opponents can barely find answers. Luka no longer just dazzles: he also inspires reverence .

It's fantastic to win by 20 against a team like Miami, it's really incredible. But it's not just me, it's everyone. Everyone is in the right places and shooting with confidence

He takes it as something normal, like someone who goes to the office every day and does his job: "When we win, the feeling is much better" , said the Slovenian genius after yet another masterclass. And he highlighted the Lakers' form and their last two wins at crypto.com Arena: "It's fantastic to beat a team like Miami by 20, it's really incredible, especially on back-to-back nights. But it's not just me, it's everyone. Everyone is in the right places and shooting with confidence" .

Giannis Antetokounmp o, the star signing of the Miami Heat and someone who knows from personal experience, because he has done it many times, how difficult it is to put up numbers like Doncic in the NBA, was in awe of the former Real Madrid player's display: "Obviously, he is one of the best scorers to have played this sport, if not the best . I'm not talking about now. I'm talking about all time," he said.

"Obviously, Luka is one of the best scorers to have ever played this sport, if not the best. I'm not talking about right now. I'm talking about all time. There are people who are afraid to say it, but he has to be among the best scorers in history

The Greek, one of the NBA's most prolific scorers since debuting with the Milwaukee Bucks in the 2013-14 season and now in his fourteenth season in the League, was the Heat's best player with 30 points (10/14 on two-pointers, 0/3 on three-pointers and 10/15 from the line), 12 rebounds, seven assists and two blocks , but his magnificent game was overshadowed by the Doncic cyclone, to whom he paid tribute. "I think there are people who are afraid to say it, but Luka has to be among the best scorers in history" . Miami coach Erik Spoelstra struck a similar note: "It's a huge challenge to go up against a genius like Doncic."

JJ Redick , coach of the Lakers , can't stop marveling at the spectacular performances, night after night, of his team's star, whose ability he highlights to make monstrous feats like the ones he achieved against the Heat look easy simply by repeating them over and over again. "It's like a supernova , although at the same time it seems like something normal," Redick explained. "We live in a spaceship, and we go at the speed of light all the time when he's on the court. When he's on fire, it's pick your poison, because he can make any shot. And then opponents start putting two on the ball, and everyone else benefits from that . He's a tremendous offensive engine."

Luka seems like a supernova; with him, we’re living in a spaceship, and we’re going at the speed of light all the time when he’s on the court. When he gets hot, it’s pick your poison, because he can make any shot

His teammates , privileged spectators who night after night witness Doncic 's displays from the front row or right beside him, still cannot quite grasp how easily he scores, even beating the double or triple teams that opponents sometimes throw at him. "It's crazy . It feels like practically any shot he takes, whether it's a circus shot, or a regular step-back three, or a difficult shot, is going in, it's like something unreal" , commented Los Angeles guard Quentin Grimes .

Luka is doing incredible things, and when he does that, he simply opens up the court so everyone else can play freely and with confidence

And Austin Reaves , his best partner on the court, is already at a loss for words in the face of the continuous feats of his great supporter on the Lakers: "Luka is doing incredible things, and when he does that, he simply opens up the floor so everyone else can play freely and with confidence" . Which basically means making life easier and better for everyone around him on his team. No wonder they put the Slovenian on a pedestal , as he is unanimously revered by his teammates, the fans, and his rivals.

articles.summary: At least one NBA official appears to have a soccer background.
articles.body:
By this point, everyone knows that Victor Wembanyama is a man of many talents. One of those talents that stood out to many fans was when video clips went viral of the 7-foot-4 Wembanyama playing soccer in Costa Rica during vacation. A man of that size shouldn't be so good with his feet.

Wemby got another chance to show off his soccer skills this week, but on the basketball court. With the San Antonio Spurs up by 25 points at the end of the third quarter against the Utah Jazz , Wemby decided to juggle a soccer ball before kicking it over to the referee.

The Frenchman has a true love for the sport of soccer, though. Whenever given the opportunity with a ball by his feet, Wemby likes showing off what could have been if he hadn't grown so tall.

articles.title: Charlie Villanueva uses the “white girlfriend” defense to deny the racial controversy in the NBA: “I didn't say that!”
articles.standfirst: Charlie Villanueva stands by controversial NBA comments despite growing criticism on social media
articles.summary: Charlie Villanueva stands by controversial NBA comments despite growing criticism on social media
articles.body:
Charlie Villanueva has found himself at the center of a heated debate about race in basketball after questioning whether a white player could ever become the face of the NBA .

His comments have attracted considerable attention, particularly because they came while Dallas Mavericks youngster Cooper Flagg continues to establish himself as one of the league’s brightest prospects.

Speaking on the To The Baha podcast alongside former NBA players, Villanueva argued that a white American player would struggle to become the league's biggest representative because of the NBA's predominantly Black playing population.

"I don’t think a white dude could be the face of the league… When was the last time a white player was single-handedly the best player?… My first n*t was with a white girl, so why would I be racist? I’m not racist,” said Villanueva .

The former Mavericks forward questioned when a white player had last been recognized as the undisputed best player in basketball. He also referenced Larry Bird , suggesting that his popularity was closely connected to his rivalry with Magic Johnson.

Villanueva's remarks quickly sparked criticism, with some interpreting them as an argument that white players couldn't reach the highest level of individual success in the NBA.

However, he later took to social media to explain that his comments had been misunderstood. He specifically highlighted the difference between being the league's best player and becoming its most recognisable public figure.

Villanueva insists Cooper Flagg and international stars aren't the issue

Responding to the growing backlash, Villanueva made it clear that he considers several white and international players among the best in the world.

He specifically mentioned Luka Doncic and Nikola Jokic , while also praising Flagg's ability and describing the young Mavericks star as elite.

Villanueva insisted that his argument wasn't about individual talent or whether white players could dominate statistically. Instead, he was questioning whether a white player could become the NBA's defining personality and representative.

His clarification, however, didn't stop people from revisiting another controversial part of his original appearance.

During the podcast discussion, Villanueva attempted to dismiss accusations of racism by making a personal reference to his romantic history. He claimed that his first sexual experience was with a white woman before questioning why anyone would consider him racist.

The unusual mention quickly became another talking point as clips from the conversation circulated online.

Comedian Sam Tripoli also joined the discussion on X, directly asking Villanueva whether he had actually made the comment about his first sexual experience with a white woman.

Rather than backing away from the statement, Villanueva confirmed it with a brief response: "Yup."

The controversy arrives at an interesting moment for Flagg , whose performances have increased expectations surrounding his future in Dallas. The 19-year-old has already demonstrated the scoring ability and confidence needed to become a major NBA attraction.

Villanueva's comments have therefore opened a wider conversation about representation in professional basketball.

articles.title: LeBron James takes a wine break after wild collision sends him into 76ers crowd
articles.standfirst: The Lakers legend knows how to keep fans entertained, even when things get a little out of hand on the court
articles.summary: The Lakers legend knows how to keep fans entertained, even when things get a little out of hand on the court
articles.body:
L eBron James is fully focused when he steps onto the basketball court, but that does not mean he cannot find ways to break the tension with moments that fans will remember. The 76ers star has shown that he knows how to entertain the crowd, even in the middle of a game, and his latest courtside interaction was another example.

Philadelphia had things under control against the Chicago Bulls, although it was not the most dominant performance of the season against a struggling opponent. The 76ers eventually pulled away late to secure the win, but J ames managed to provide one of the night's most talked-about moments along the way.

A courtside moment worth remembering

The moment that stole the spotlight came after James collided with the crowd and found himself close to a fan holding a glass of wine . LeBron played along by pretending to take a sip, giving the impression that he was enjoying a quick wine break in the middle of the action . He did not actually drink from the fan's glass, but t he gesture was enough to get people talking.

This is not the first time James has pretended to enjoy an alcoholic drink while sitting courtside. His playful side has become part of his personality, and he continues to find ways to connect with fans beyond what he does during the game.

LeBron is making his presence felt in Philadelphia

Although James is no longer the same player he was during his prime, he has still proven to be a valuable addition to the 76ers this season. His basketball IQ and ability to attack in transition has added another dimension to Philadelphia's offense . He has also taken a step forward defensively compared to what fans saw from him during his final seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers.

Moments like this also show that James wants to win over the Philadelphia crowd both on and off the court. Beyond his contribution to the team's performance, building that connection with the fans is another way to make his arrival worthwhile . The 76ers improved to 7-1 in the 2026-27 NBA season after defeating Chicago, and LeBron has already found ways to make his presence felt.

articles.title: Savannah James reveals what her family is going through after LeBron moved out of the house
articles.standfirst: The NBA star's move has forced the family to rethink their routine, with Savannah now juggling life across multiple cities
articles.summary: The NBA star's move has forced the family to rethink their routine, with Savannah now juggling life across multiple cities
articles.body:
T he James family is going through a complicated period, but they are finding ways to make it work through organization and a willingness to adapt. Savannah James opened up about the situation during a conversation with Keke Palmer , admitting that trying to keep everything together has been stressful as they adjust to LeBron James' move to Philadelphia.

Although the family has the resources to travel across the country whenever necessary, time remains something they cannot control . With everyone following different paths, they are now trying to balance their lives between New York, Philadelphia, Los Angeles and Tucson. Being able to move from one city to another does not mean they can be everywhere at once, so finding a routine that works for everyone has become a full-time job.

Zhuri's decision changed the family's plans

One of the biggest adjustments came from their daughter Zhuri, who decided to stay in Los Angeles rather than move with her father . While she had initially been concerned about not seeing LeBron as often, she ultimately chose to remain close to her friends and continue playing volleyball with the team she has been part of since she was young.

The family respected her decision, allowing her to maintain the friendships and athletic commitments she has built in Los Angeles. Like her father and brothers, Zhuri is already developing her own path in sports , and staying with her volleyball team was an important part of that.

Savannah is balancing everyone's different priorities

Savannah explained the situation in a relaxed manner, although she did not hide how much coordination it requires . LeBron chose to move to Philadelphia while living in New York, Zhuri preferred Los Angeles over New York, Bronny remains committed to the Lakers, and Bryce is in Tucson attending the University of Arizona as he continues building his own future.

That leaves Savannah managing the different schedules and locations while trying to keep the family connected. It could be argued that she is the one making the biggest adjustments to accommodate everyone's decisions , since each member has chosen a different direction.

A full-time job keeping the family together

Savannah described the process of organizing their lives as a full-time job. The arrangement feels different from what they were used to, and she acknowledged that it can be stressful, but she is taking things one day at a time and believes they will find a way to make it work.

Her approach has earned praise from those who recognize the role she plays in keeping the family together . With LeBron's unexpected move changing their routine and the children pursuing their own commitments, Savannah has become a central part of making this complicated arrangement work without requiring everyone to be in the same place.

articles.title: Luka Doncic is on a scoring tear. Could this finally be his year to win an NBA championship?
articles.standfirst: The Slovenian player showed that he can dominate a game while creating opportunities for everyone around him
articles.summary: The Slovenian player showed that he can dominate a game while creating opportunities for everyone around him
articles.body:
L uka Doncic is putting together the kind of offensive stretch that can make the Los Angeles Lakers believe they have a legitimate shot at an NBA championship. Just two weeks into a new season, the Slovenian superstar is scoring at a historic pace, elevating his teammates and giving the franchise a compelling reason to believe it can contend in the post-LeBron James era.

Doncic's latest statement came in consecutive victories over the Toronto Raptors and Miami Heat. He scored 45 points and grabbed 15 rebounds against Toronto on Sunday before delivering 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds in Monday night's comfortable win over Miami.

Those performances were more than another pair of spectacular scoring nights. They demonstrated how Doncic can dominate a game while creating opportunities for everyone around him, a combination that could prove decisive if the Lakers hope to make a deep postseason run. “Obviously, it feels good (to score), but when you win by 20 against a team like Miami, it's really awesome, especially on a back-to-back,” Doncic said.

The Lakers are 6-2 despite introducing nine new players to the roster, and their early results suggest the transition to a team built around Doncic is progressing quickly. The question now is whether his individual brilliance can translate into the ultimate prize: his first NBA championship.

Doncic is scoring at an extraordinary rate

Luka has scored at least 37 points in five consecutive games, surpassing 40 points in four of them. During that stretch, he has made 34 three-pointers while shooting 53.1% from the field. The run began with a 52-point performance against Utah, followed by games of 41 and 37 points. Although the Lakers lost those two contests, Doncic's subsequent performances against Toronto and Miami helped turn his scoring explosion into a winning streak.

For a player entering his ninth NBA season, the production is remarkable. Doncic has already won two of the previous three NBA scoring titles, and his early-season surge has put him at the forefront of the race for another.

His game remains built around the skills that have made him one of basketball's most difficult players to defend: step-back three-pointers, creative passes, an ability to manipulate defensive coverages and an uncanny knack for converting difficult shots.

But the most encouraging development for Los Angeles is that Luka's impact is extending beyond the scoreboard. Lakers guard Quentin Grimes has seen the scoring spree up close and admitted that Dončić's shot-making has become almost impossible to believe.

When a superstar reaches that level, opposing defenses have few attractive options. Give Doncic space, and he can score from virtually anywhere. Send additional defenders, and he can turn the resulting openings into easy opportunities for his teammates. That dilemma is already becoming the defining feature of the Lakers' offense.

The Lakers are learning how to capitalize on his brilliance

Los Angeles coach JJ Redick has described the experience of watching Doncic operate as something extraordinary, even by NBA standards. “We live on a spaceship, and we're going at the speed of light at all times when he's on the court,” Redick said. “When he has it going, it's pick your poison, because he can just make any shot. And then you start putting two on the ball, and everybody else is the beneficiary of that.”

The Lakers' recent performances have illustrated that dynamic. Opponents have increasingly sent two or even three defenders toward Doncic well beyond the three-point line, hoping to force the ball out of his hands before he can create a scoring opportunity. Instead, he has repeatedly found the open man.

Los Angeles made 37 of 80 three-point attempts across its victories over Toronto and Miami while scoring 269 combined points. Against the Heat, the Lakers recorded 39 assists, their highest total in a game since Redick took over as head coach in 2024.

Those numbers suggest an offense becoming more dangerous than a one-man scoring show. Doncic's ability to draw multiple defenders creates space for shooters, opens passing lanes and makes it more difficult for opponents to concentrate their defensive attention on a single threat.

The bodycam footage captures a strange pause in a serious traffic stop. J.R. Smith was talking with Royse City officers about his NBA career when one of them brought up LeBron James . The officer called him “He who shall not be named.” Smith asked, “Not a fan?” The reply: “He stole Luka from us. That was all him.”

The comment was about the 2025 trade that sent Luka Doncic from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers . The officer’s “theft” remark was a fan’s grievance about the deal, not a formal accusation. Reporting at the time said James was stunned by the trade; he later said he spent two days in disbelief.

The conversation unfolded during Smith’s arrest

The stop took place Sept. 28 on Interstate 30 in Royse City, Texas. Police pulled over the vehicle after a license plate alert flagged an outstanding warrant.

While officers checked Smith’s information, the conversation turned to his NBA career and his two championships with Cleveland in 2016 and the Lakers in 2020, both alongside James.

Officers then confirmed the warrant and arrested him. The footage became public Nov. 3; the arrest itself was not new.

The warrant was tied to a charge of assault causing bodily injury involving family violence, stemming from an alleged Sept. 18 incident. Smith was released on a $5,000 bond the following day. A judge also signed an emergency protective order restricting contact with the woman involved.

Smith’s attorney, Justin A. Moore, said Smith is presumed innocent and that the case would be addressed in court.

After 16 seasons in the NBA , the former guard pursued a different path: he enrolled at North Carolina A&T, joined its men’s golf team and earned a degree in liberal studies in 2025.

The footage lasts only a few seconds , but the allegation behind the arrest concerns real people and carries consequences far beyond what a bodycam can show.

The case remains unresolved. Smith is presumed innocent , and his attorney says it will be addressed in court; the privacy of everyone involved deserves respect.

Although the officer is still angry with LeBron James and believes he was the one to blame.
